task.title: Pick a free port automatically when the default board address is taken
task.description:
workbook serve defaults its listener to 127.0.0.1:7331 (internal/cli/run.go:809). net.Listen on an occupied port fails immediately with the "open board listener" operational error (run.go:864-867), so running boards for two local projects means the second serve dies unless the user remembers to pass --addr with a hand-picked port. Multiple repositories using Workbook on one machine is an expected setup; the second board should just start.

Fix: when the user did not pass --addr explicitly, treat 7331 as a preference, not a requirement. Try it first so the common single-project case keeps its stable, bookmarkable URL; if the bind fails because the address is in use, fall back to an OS-assigned ephemeral port (port 0). The groundwork is already in place — the startup banner prints the resolved address via listener.Addr() (run.go:868), so an ephemeral port surfaces to the user with no other change. When the user did pass --addr explicitly, keep failing loudly: an explicit address is a contract, and silently drifting to another port would break whatever the user pointed at it.

Acceptance criteria:
- With no board running, workbook serve still binds 127.0.0.1:7331 and prints that address.
- With one board already on 7331, a second workbook serve in another repository starts successfully on an OS-assigned port and prints the actual address it bound.
- The fallback triggers only on address-in-use; other bind failures (e.g. permission denied on a privileged port) still fail with the operational error.
- workbook serve --addr with an explicit address that is occupied still fails with the existing error rather than falling back.
- Tests cover the fallback path (occupy 7331 in the test, assert the second listener binds elsewhere) and the explicit-address failure path.
- The --addr flag help text documents the fallback behavior of the default.
